chapters.title: 1. Synonyms
chapters.notes:
### 1.1 How synonyms are asked
- Format 1: "Choose the word nearest in meaning to ___". Format 2: a sentence with an underlined word to replace.
- Trick: first make your own meaning in Bengali, then look at the options. Eliminate options with the opposite feeling (positive vs negative).
- Watch roots: bene = good (benevolent), mal = bad (malign), phil = love, mis = hate, omni = all, chron = time, loqu = speak.
- Exam rule: in IDO, English is 15 MCQs. Vocabulary (synonym, antonym, one word, idiom) usually gives 6-8 of them. Each wrong answer costs 0.25.

chapters.title: 2. Antonyms
chapters.notes:
### 2.1 How to solve
- Find the meaning, flip it, then match. Two options are often a synonym trap: do not pick the synonym.
- Prefixes that make opposites: un- (unhappy), in-/im-/il-/ir- (inactive, impossible, illegal, irregular), dis- (dislike), non- (non-violent), mis- (misuse).
- im- before b, m, p (imbalance, immature, impossible); il- before l (illegal); ir- before r (irregular).
- PYQ: The opposite of "Balance" made with a prefix = Imbalance (not "unbalance" as a noun).

chapters.title: 3. One-word Substitution
chapters.notes:
### 3.1 Root families (learn the ending, get many words)
| Ending | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| -cide | killing | homicide (man), suicide (self), regicide (king), patricide (father), matricide (mother), fratricide (brother), sororicide (sister), infanticide (infant), genocide (race), uxoricide (wife), pesticide, insecticide |
| -cracy | rule by | democracy (people), autocracy (one person), theocracy (priests), plutocracy (rich), bureaucracy (officials), aristocracy (nobles), gerontocracy (old people), kleptocracy (thieves) |
| -archy | rule | monarchy (king), anarchy (no rule), oligarchy (a few), matriarchy / patriarchy |
| - phobia | fear of | hydrophobia (water), claustrophobia (closed space), acrophobia (height), agoraphobia (open/public place), nyctophobia (darkness), xenophobia (foreigners), astraphobia (thunder) |
| -logy | study of | ornithology (birds), entomology (insects), anthropology (man), etymology (word origin), seismology (earthquakes), oology (eggs), numismatics (coins; not -logy!), philately (stamps) |
| -gamy | marriage | monogamy (one), bigamy (two at a time), polygamy (many), misogamy (hatred of marriage) |
| - vorous | eating | herbivorous (plants), carnivorous (flesh), omnivorous (everything), insectivorous (insects) |

chapters.title: 5. Prepositions & Fixed Usage
chapters.notes:
### 5.1 Basic rules
- A preposition shows the relation of a noun/pronoun with another word: in, on, at, by, with, for, of, to, from, into...
- Time: at a point (at 5 pm, at night), on day/date (on Monday, on 15 August), in month/year/season/part of day (in May, in 2026, in the morning).
- Since vs For: since + point of time (since 2010), for + period (for two years).
- Between two; among more than two. Beside = by the side of; besides = in addition to.
- In = state of rest inside; into = motion inside (He jumped into the river).
- By for doer/means (by bus, written by Tagore); with for instrument (cut with a knife).
- PYQ: It is 9 o'clock by my watch. He has a preference for tea over coffee. Ram made the most of his resources.
### 5.2 Words followed by fixed prepositions (from the manual)
| Preposition | Words that take it |
|---|---|
| with | merge, argue, share, trade, coexist, clash, compete, haggle, work, row, bargain, fight, struggle, disagree, interact, ally, wrangle |
| to | confide, complain, turn, offer, convert, disloyal, devoted, allergic, sympathetic, unfair, loyal, unkind, explain, write, indebted, indifferent, immune, central, impervious |
| into | trick, blossom, seduce, turn, deceive, divide, evolve, convert, galvanise, pressurise, coerce |
| about | phobia, wonder, quarrel, angry, joke, enthusiastic, crazy, ignorant, complacent, certain, question |
| against | agitate, compete, plot, protect, warn, insure, militate, vaccinate, shield, war, campaign, defence, blow, fight, crime, victory |
| for | love, nostalgia, mania, lust, affection, weakness, thirst, respect, hope, liking, longing, apology |
| in | specialise, delight, pride, interest, deal, indulge, fluctuation, rise, fall, share, success |
| on | rely, depend, insist, comment, congratulate, focus, embark, impose, concentrate |
| of | afraid, aware, capable, fond, guilty, proud, ashamed, conscious, devoid, full, sure, tired |

### 5.3 More fixed phrases
| abide by | accuse of | adhere to | agree with (person) | agree to (proposal) |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| angry with (person) / at (thing) | assure of | blind to | comply with | consist of |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| die of (disease) / from (cause) | differ from | good at | married to | prefer to |

| prevent from | senior / junior to | superior / inferior to |
|---|---|---|

- Note: "senior, junior, superior, inferior, prefer" take to , not "than". Example: He is senior to me.

chapters.title: 6. Grammar Essentials from PYQs
chapters.notes:
### 6.1 Tenses
- Present perfect (have/has + V3) with "already, just, yet, ever, never, since, for". Never use it with a past time word (yesterday, last night, ago).
- Past perfect (had + V3) for the earlier of two past actions: The train had left before I reached.
- PYQ 2019: "We had gone to the movies last night" is wrong → We went to the movies last night / "I am sure I have met him before" / "I have known him for a long time."
- No sooner ... than with inversion: No sooner had the sun risen than the fog disappeared. Also Hardly /Scarcely ... when.
- Conditional: If + past perfect → would have + V3 (If he had worked hard, he would have passed).
### 6.2 Subject-verb agreement
- Two subjects joined by and → plural verb. But "Bread and butter is my breakfast" (one idea).
- Each, every, either, neither, everyone, one of the ... → singular verb: One of the boys is absent.
- Collective noun (jury, team, committee): one unit → singular; members acting separately → plural.
- PYQ: The jury were divided in their opinion.
- Neither ... nor / Either ... or / not only ... but also → verb agrees with the nearer subject.
- The number of → singular; A number of → plural.
### 6.3 Voice & Narration
| Active | Passive |
|---|---|
| He writes a letter. | A letter is written by him. |
| He is writing a letter. | A letter is being written by him. |
| He has written a letter. | A letter has been written by him. |
| He wrote a letter. | A letter was written by him. |
| He will write a letter. | A letter will be written by him. |
| Open the door. | Let the door be opened. |

- PYQ: "The script is being written." → Active: They are writing the script.
- Narration: said to → told / asked / ordered; present → past (am → was, will → would); here → there, now → then, today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the previous day.
- Universal truths do not change tense: The teacher said that the earth moves round the sun.
### 6.4 Articles, conjunctions & common confusions
- A before consonant sound (a university, a European, a one-rupee coin); An before vowel sound (an hour, an honest man, an MLA).
- The before unique things, rivers, oceans, mountain ranges, superlatives, newspapers (the Ganga, the Himalayas, the best).
- Until (time) vs unless (condition). Though ... yet; Lest ... should (Walk carefully lest you should fall).
- Sometime (at some point), some time (a period), sometimes (now and then). PYQ: Let's meet sometime next week.
- Later (time), latter (second of two). PYQ: He entered the hall in the latter part of the show.
- Notwithstanding = in spite of. PYQ: Notwithstanding his humiliation, he attended the function.
- Interjections: Alas! (sorrow / regret), Hurrah! (joy), Bravo! (praise), Hush! (silence).
### 6.5 Sentence conversion (PYQ type)
- Compound → simple: "She wanted to go on vacation, so she saved money" → She saved money for vacation.
- "Pancakes are delicious but not without syrup" → Pancakes are delicious only with syrup.
- Assertive → interrogative: "I will meet you at the train station" → Where will you meet me? (the question whose answer is the place).
- Error-spotting checklist: 1) subject-verb agreement 2) tense with time word 3) preposition 4)
- article 5) pronoun case (between you and me ) 6) degree of comparison (more better ✗).
